novel.justification: This is this proposal's compact model-class restriction for uniform bounds, not a condition attributed to Dettling, Drton, and Kolar. It holds on any fixed compact subset of the positive-definite covariance cone, including standardized Gaussian equilibrium families whose covariance eigenvalues remain in a prespecified interval.

assumptions.condition: The selected common-time-scale representative satisfies \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\) and \(D(d)=\operatorname{diag}(d,1-d)\).

novel.justification: This proposal derives the normalization from the common time-scale orbit. If \(\widetilde A\Sigma+\Sigma\widetilde A^{\top}=\widetilde D\) and \(c=1/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), then \((c\widetilde A)\Sigma+\Sigma(c\widetilde A)^{\top}=c\widetilde D\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(c\widetilde D)=1\). Equivalently, in generator-sign form the direct algebra is \((-\widetilde A)\Sigma+\Sigma(-\widetilde A)^{\top}+\widetilde D=0\Rightarrow(-c\widetilde A)\Sigma+\Sigma(-c\widetilde A)^{\top}+c\widetilde D=0\). The constants \(\eta\) and \(M\) are bounds in the normalized time unit selected by this gauge.

assumptions.condition: The mean-reversion matrix and covariance obey \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D\).

standard.name: continuous Lyapunov stationarity equation under the mean-reversion sign convention

assumptions.condition: In the normalized time unit selected by \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), the first directed coefficient satisfies \(|A_{12}|\ge\eta\).

standard.name: beta-min separation for the first directed edge

assumptions.condition: In the normalized time unit selected by \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), the second directed coefficient satisfies \(|A_{21}|\ge\eta\).

standard.name: beta-min separation for the second directed edge

assumptions.condition: In the normalized time unit selected by \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), the drift satisfies \(\lVert A\rVert_F\le M\).
The covariance admits at least one legal parameter pair, \(\mathcal F(\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\).

standard.name: observed law restricted to the possible set

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(\Sigma\), the observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent with common law \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\).

standard.name: independent equilibrium snapshots from a Gaussian OU process

definitions.name: closed joint-sign sector
definitions.construction: For \(\sigma=(\sigma_b,\sigma_c)\in\{-1,+1\}^2\), \(H_{\sigma}=\{(d,q)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R:\sigma_bA_{12}(d,q;\Sigma)\ge\eta,\ \sigma_cA_{21}(d,q;\Sigma)\ge\eta\}\), and \(J_{\sigma}\) is the assertion that some \((d,q)\in H_{\sigma}\) has \(0<d<1\).

definitions.name: sector norm program
definitions.construction: Write \(f(d,q)=z^{\top}Gz+2h^{\top}z+c_0\) for \(z=(d,q)^{\top}\), with \(G=\Delta^{-2}\begin{pmatrix}(s^2+u^2+2t^2)/4&t(s+u)\\t(s+u)&s^2+u^2+2t^2\end{pmatrix}\), \(h=\Delta^{-2}(-(s^2+t^2)/4,-t(s+u)/2)^{\top}\), and \(H_{\sigma}=\{z:C_{\sigma}z\ge a_{\sigma}\}\) using the four rows \((1,0)\), \((-1,0)\), \(\sigma_b(-t/(2\Delta),-s/\Delta)\), and \(\sigma_c(t/(2\Delta),u/\Delta)\) with thresholds \(0\), \(-1\), \(\eta\), and \(\eta+\sigma_ct/(2\Delta)\).

definitions.name: stratified active-set proof handle
definitions.construction: Use the face lattice of the four halfspaces defining \(H_{\sigma}\): test the unconstrained stationary point, every stationary point on one independent active line, and every intersection of two independent active lines; then separate closed minimization from the existence of an interior point with \(0<d<1\) by convex interpolation.

definitions.name: finite equality-active candidate family
definitions.construction: Let \(z_0=-G^{-1}h\). For each independent \(I\subseteq\{1,2,3,4\}\) with \(1\le|I|\le2\), set \(z_I=z_0+G^{-1}C_I^{\top}(C_IG^{-1}C_I^{\top})^{-1}(a_I-C_Iz_0)\); retain \(z_0\) and the \(z_I\) that satisfy all four sector inequalities.

definitions.name: covariance-inverted polarity confidence set
definitions.construction: Let \(B_n=\{\Theta\in\mathcal K:\lVert\Theta-S_n\rVert_F\le r_n\}\). Set \(\Gamma_n=\bigcup_{\Theta\in B_n}\mathcal P(\Theta)\) when \(B_n\ne\varnothing\), and \(\Gamma_n=\mathcal P(\Theta_{j_n(S_n)})\) otherwise, where \(j_n(S)=\min\{j:\lVert\Theta_j-S\rVert_F<\rho(S)+1/n\}\) and \(\rho(S)=\inf_{\Theta\in\mathcal K}\lVert\Theta-S\rVert_F\).

definitions.name: regular-contact Gaussian alternatives
definitions.construction: For \(\Sigma_*\in C\subseteq\{\Sigma\in U:g(\Sigma)=0\}\), fixed \(h>0\), and \(H=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), set \(\Sigma_n^{-}=\Sigma_*-hH/\sqrt n\) and \(\Sigma_n^{+}=\Sigma_*+hH/\sqrt n\).

statements.statement: Suppose \(\widetilde D\) is diagonal and strictly positive and \(\widetilde A\Sigma+\Sigma\widetilde A^{\top}=\widetilde D\). With \(\lambda=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), the common rescaling \(A=\widetilde A/\lambda\) and \(D=\widetilde D/\lambda\) preserves \(\Sigma\), satisfies \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), and preserves \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\). It is the unique representative of the positive common-scaling class with trace-one diffusion.
statements.justification: The lemma separates an observationally irrelevant common time-unit choice from the substantive edge-margin and norm restrictions.
statements.gap: The trace-one restriction is a gauge choice for this bounded-fiber analysis, not a modeling condition attributed to the one-edge sign-identification literature.
statements.consumer: Every sector, threshold, contact, and inference result can be interpreted for an arbitrary strictly positive diagonal diffusion after converting \(\eta\) and \(M\) to the normalized time unit.

statements.statement: Every solution of \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D(d)\) has the unique representation \[A(d,q;\Sigma)=\frac1\Delta\begin{pmatrix}du/2+qt&-dt/2-qs\\-(1-d)t/2+qu&(1-d)s/2-qt\end{pmatrix}.\] Conversely, every \((d,q)\in(0,1)\times\mathbb R\) in this representation solves the Lyapunov equation and has eigenvalues with strictly positive real parts, so \(-A\) is Hurwitz.
statements.justification: The affine fiber turns a nonidentified matrix inverse problem into a two-coordinate exact feasibility problem.
statements.gap: DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023 identifies the two-cycle rank defect but does not give this time-gauged unknown-diffusion parametrization as a polarity-analysis object.
statements.consumer: The four sector programs and every explicit witness use this common coordinate system.

statements.statement: Can the stratified active-set handle be made into a complete proof that, for every admissible \(\Sigma\) and every \(\sigma\), the retained family \(\{z_0,z_I:|I|\le2\}\) contains the unique minimizer of \(f\) over every nonempty \(H_{\sigma}\), including rank-deficient line and point sectors, and that the resulting \(J_{\sigma}\) and norm-equality branches are necessary and sufficient for legal strict-diffusion feasibility?
statements.justification: This is the proof-boundary bottleneck: continuity from full-dimensional sectors does not settle strict or lower-dimensional equality branches.
statements.gap: Neither the algebraic identifiability proof of DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023 nor the one-edge feasibility argument of vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 proves this finite joint-sector certificate.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution certifies every later phase-diagram, contact, and inference claim without numerical active-set assumptions.

statements.statement: For each \(\sigma\), let \(z_{\sigma}\) be the unique minimizer of \(f\) on nonempty \(H_{\sigma}\), with \(v_{\sigma}=f(z_{\sigma})\). The sector contains a legal model if and only if \(H_{\sigma}\ne\varnothing\), \(J_{\sigma}\) holds, and \[v_{\sigma}<M^2\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl(v_{\sigma}=M^2\ \text{and}\ 0<(z_{\sigma})_d<1\bigr).\] Moreover, for \(\omega\in\{-1,+1\}\), \(H_{(\omega,\omega)}\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(-\omega t\max(s,u)\ge2\eta\Delta(s+u)\), and \(J_{(\omega,\omega)}\) holds if and only if the inequality is strict or \(s=u\) at equality; both opposite-sign sectors always satisfy \(J_{\sigma}\). Hence \(+1\in\mathcal P(\Sigma)\) exactly when one same-sign sector passes the certificate, and \(-1\in\mathcal P(\Sigma)\) exactly when one opposite-sign sector passes it.
statements.justification: The theorem is the exact necessary-and-sufficient kernel and records open versus closed attainment instead of reporting an optimization infimum.
statements.gap: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 gives an individual-edge zero criterion, while this theorem characterizes the joint product sign under simultaneous post-gauge magnitude and norm restrictions; trace one only selects the common time unit.
statements.consumer: A bivariate graphical continuous Lyapunov analysis can report every loop polarity compatible with its covariance and declared scientific bounds.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Sigma=\Sigma_r\) and \(|r|\le1-\kappa\). Then a positive-polarity legal model exists if and only if \(|r|\ge4\eta(1-r^2)\) and \(M^2\ge C_r\). A negative-polarity legal model exists if and only if \(M^2>V_-(r)\), or \(M^2=V_-(r)\) and \(|r|L_r<(1-r^2)/4\). At \(r=1/2\), \(\eta=3/5\), and \(M^2=67/45\), the negative-sector closed infimum is unattained under \(0<d<1\).
statements.justification: The slice yields analytic thresholds and separates attained margin equality from unattained norm equality.
statements.gap: Hansen2025Trek derives variance inequalities for acyclic models; no cited result gives cyclic product-sign thresholds or their strict-attainment branch.
statements.consumer: The formulas give exact calibration and regression tests for implementations of the general certificate.

statements.statement: For \(\kappa=1/2\), \(\eta=1/10\), and \(M=1\), there is an open neighborhood \(U_I\) of \(I_2\) contained in \(\mathcal K\) such that \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{-1\}\) for every \(\Sigma\in U_I\), while each of \(A_{12}\) and \(A_{21}\) takes both signs across \(\mathcal F(\Sigma)\).
statements.justification: This proves that graph-level polarity contains information absent from either edge sign on a nondegenerate region.
statements.gap: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 establishes positive-measure edge-sign regimes but does not exhibit joint-only identification of a feedback product.
statements.consumer: Qualitative feedback classification remains defensible when the direction of each individual interaction is not.

statements.statement: At the constants in \(\mathrm{def:contact}\), there exists an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(\Sigma_0\), contained in the strict covariance bounds and in \(\mathcal K\), such that \[\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{-1\}\ \text{when }g(\Sigma)\le0,\qquad \mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{-1,+1\}\ \text{when }g(\Sigma)>0.\] On \(U\), \(s>u\), \(t>0\), and \(\partial g/\partial t>0\). At \(\Sigma_0\), the positive sector has only the closed witness \(d=0\), \(A_{12}=A_{21}=-\eta\), with \(\lVert A\rVert_F<M\); for \(g(\Sigma)>0\), the assignments \(d=g(\Sigma)/(2(s-u)t)\) and \(q=(\eta\Delta-dt/2)/s\) give legal positive-product witnesses after shrinking \(U\).
statements.justification: The theorem exposes a smooth statistical boundary generated by strict diffusion positivity rather than by a binding drift norm.
statements.gap: The cited Lyapunov identification papers analyze algebraic or generic failures and do not identify an explicit zero-diffusion polarity contact with open adjacent regimes.
statements.consumer: The contact supplies a transparent stress test for inference and a local coordinate for sharp recovery theory.

statements.statement: Assume \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\). The random set \(\Gamma_n\) is measurable and nonempty, and for every \(n\ge1\), \[\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\mathcal P(\Sigma)\subseteq\Gamma_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
statements.justification: The result gives honest finite-sample coverage of the entire compatible sign set, including nonclosed model branches.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 provides general set-inversion theory, while vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 has no sampling result; the measurable empty-intersection fallback is specific to this strict OU model.
statements.consumer: A reported bivariate feedback sign set has a finite-sample frequentist guarantee rather than a brittle plug-in label.

statements.statement: For every sequence \(a_n\to\infty\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K\) with \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{a\}\) and \(\delta_a(\Sigma)\ge a_n/\sqrt n\), \(\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\Gamma_n=\{a\}\}\to1\). More precisely, when \(\delta_a(\Sigma)>2r_n\) and \(\delta_a(\Sigma)>2/n\), the failure probability is at most \(16V/(n\delta_a(\Sigma)^2)\).
statements.justification: Coverage becomes informative away from the opposing-sign frontier at the regular covariance-estimation scale.
statements.gap: No cited OU paper proves uniform exact-set recovery; generic set inversion does not resolve the nearest-model branch when \(B_n\) is empty.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain a transparent clearance condition under which the honest set collapses to the identified polarity.

statements.statement: For every compact \(C\subseteq\{\Sigma\in U:g(\Sigma)=0\}\), there are a neighborhood \(W\) of \(C\) with \(\overline W\subset U\) and constants \(0<c<C_1<\infty\) such that, for \(\Sigma\in W\) with \(g(\Sigma)\le0\), \[\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma,K_{+1})=\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma,\{\Theta\in U:g(\Theta)=0\}),\qquad c|g(\Sigma)|\le\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma,K_{+1})\le C_1|g(\Sigma)|.\]
statements.justification: The statement connects the explicit algebraic certificate margin to the metric clearance used by the recovery theorem.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 supplies general tangent-cone tools but not this one-sided OU boundary-distance equivalence or the buffer excluding remote model components.
statements.consumer: Certificate-based clearance can be interpreted and calibrated as local covariance distance on regular contact subcharts.

statements.statement: For every \(\Sigma_*\in C\) and fixed \(h>0\), the alternatives \(\Sigma_n^{-}\) and \(\Sigma_n^{+}\) lie in \(U\cap\mathcal K\) for all large \(n\), satisfy \(\mathcal P(\Sigma_n^{-})=\{-1\}\) and \(\mathcal P(\Sigma_n^{+})=\{-1,+1\}\), and have \(\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma_n^{-},K_{+1})\asymp n^{-1/2}\). Their \(n\)-snapshot Gaussian experiments are mutually contiguous, uniformly for \(\Sigma_*\) on compact contact subcharts. Consequently, any procedure \(\widetilde\Gamma_n\) satisfying asymptotic uniform coverage of \(\mathcal P\) at level \(1-\alpha\) has \(\liminf\Pr_{\Sigma_n^{-}}\{+1\in\widetilde\Gamma_n\}>0\) along these sequences and cannot recover the singleton uniformly at root-\(n\) contact distance.
statements.justification: The lower bound shows that the clearance rate in the upper theorem is locally sharp for honest procedures.
statements.gap: Kaji2021 gives general weak-identification impossibility, but the reduced-form coordinate, contact geometry, and Gaussian covariance divergence are new to this OU target.
statements.consumer: The result prevents claims of uniformly faster singleton classification and identifies the appropriate reporting regime near contact.

sampling_model.design: Independent cross-sectional equilibrium sampling from \(dX_t=-AX_tdt+D^{1/2}dW_t\), with known zero mean; \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\) selects a representative under common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the generator coefficients are \(-A_{12}\) and \(-A_{21}\), whose product has the same sign as \(A_{12}A_{21}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; strict diffusion positivity and covariance eigenvalue bounds replace treatment overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The regular nuisance is \(\Sigma\), estimated by \(S_n\); drift and diffusion are not selected pointwise but are existentially profiled through the sector certificate, with \(\eta\) and \(M\) interpreted in the normalized time unit.

estimand_functional: \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{+1:\text{a same-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\cup\{-1:\text{an opposite-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.2 characterizes pointwise ambiguity of one target edge by membership in its zero-edge signature set.
Global drift identifiability with diagonal volatility holds exactly for simple graphs, and the directed two-cycle has a nontrivial fiber.
The Lyapunov trek rule yields a power-series covariance expansion and acyclic variance inequalities.
Model equivalence and structural identifiability are characterized for acyclic graphical continuous Lyapunov models.
An \(\ell_1\)-regularized Lyapunov estimator has model-selection guarantees under an irrepresentability condition.
Criterion inversion yields confidence regions, consistency, and rates for identified sets.
Directional differentiability determines when the standard bootstrap fails and supports locally valid alternatives.
Weakly regular parameters admit local impossibility results through underlying regular parameters.
Higher-order cumulant equations generically identify the drift under non-Gaussianity and support asymptotically normal estimation.

tldr: Stationary Gaussian snapshots identify a covariance but not the drift around a directed feedback cycle when diagonal diffusion is unknown. The project selects one representative of the common time-scale class by imposing \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\), interprets \(\eta\) and \(M\) in those normalized units, and characterizes exactly which values of \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\) occur on the resulting bounded bivariate Lyapunov fiber. Its focal object is a four-sector certificate that distinguishes feasible, closure-only, and infeasible branches, including equal-variance thresholds and an asymmetric zero-diffusion contact. Covariance-region inversion then gives honest finite-sample set coverage, uniform singleton recovery beyond \(n^{-1/2}\) clearance, and a matching local Gaussian obstruction on compact regular contact subcharts.

project_justification.gap: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar characterize signs one drift edge at a time and explicitly leave subgraph and graph-level signs open. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen identify the directed two-cycle as the obstruction to full drift recovery under fixed diagonal volatility, but do not characterize a coarser sign quotient along its affine Lyapunov fiber. Neither result resolves strict-diffusion attainment or sampling uncertainty at the resulting contact sets.
project_justification.niche: The exactly bivariate cycle is the smallest model in which full drift identification fails while a joint causal feature can remain point identified. Common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\) changes only time units and leaves the stationary covariance and cycle polarity unchanged; trace one fixes that gauge, while \(\eta\) and \(M\) are bounds in the selected units rather than scale-free restrictions.
project_justification.fill: The project first records the common time-scale equivalence and its unique trace-one representative, then derives an exact finite semialgebraic certificate for the compatible loop-polarity set, proves its open-versus-closed branches, gives closed-form equal-variance and asymmetric-contact reductions, and propagates the population set through a Gaussian covariance confidence region with local sharpness at regular contacts.

related_work: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar (2026, Theorem 4.2, Remark 5.1, and the Conclusion) introduce one-edge signature sets, reduce their feasibility to linear restrictions, and explicitly identify graph-level signs as an open direction; their positive diagonal diffusion setting informs the target map but does not supply or require the trace-one convention used here. Trace one is solely the representative selected by common rescaling of \(A\) and \(D\), and \(\eta\) and \(M\) are imposed after that choice of time units. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen (2023, Example 3.2 and Theorem 4.3) show that the directed two-cycle generates the sharp failure of global drift identification with diagonal volatility; their half-vectorized Lyapunov map informs the affine-fiber reduction. Hansen (2025) gives a trek expansion and acyclic variance inequalities, while the cyclic inverse fiber and its strict boundary topology are outside that result. Dettling, Drton, and Kolar (2024) analyze Lyapunov-lasso model selection from equilibrium snapshots rather than inference on a known graph's compatible sign quotient. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) inform confidence-region inversion for set-valued parameters. Fang and Santos (2019) inform nonsmooth boundary analysis, and Kaji (2021) informs the local weak-identification interpretation. Recke and Hansen (2026) recover the full drift using non-Gaussian higher cumulants; Gaussian snapshots remove precisely that extra information and leave the polarity fiber studied here.
technical_internal_limitation: The complete equality-active-set proof is the load-bearing unresolved step. It must cover dependent constraint rows, sectors that are lines or points, same-sign equality with \(s=u\), interior-diffusion failure at \(d\in\{0,1\}\), and norm equality without invoking Slater continuity. The early kill tests are the asymmetric \(g=0\) contact with false \(J\), an attained positive equal-variance threshold, and the unattained negative infimum at \(r=1/2\), \(\eta=3/5\), and \(M^2=67/45\). Failure of any branch stops the theorem spine.
honest_scope: The project is exactly bivariate and observational. It excludes larger-graph projection, marginalization, empirical performance, and global equivalence between certificate margin and covariance distance. The trace-one restriction fixes common time units only; the substantive magnitude bounds \(\eta\) and \(M\) must be converted whenever a different time unit is used. The population certificate and its inference consequences remain to be proved. The local distance and lower-bound claims are confined to compact regular subcharts of the explicit asymmetric contact. As a reduction outside the two-edge beta-min class, delete one directed edge and its margin condition. The resulting simple cause--effect graph has \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12})=-\operatorname{sign}(t)\) under the present mean-reversion convention, which is the one-edge covariance-sign formula of van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar after converting their generator sign convention.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct both opposite-sign orientations with common strict slack, then separately exclude both same-sign sectors through the joint elimination identity.

seed_details.red_team: The product is identified only at the isolated covariance \(I_2\).

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Embed the cumulant equations in a local sequence whose third-or-higher cumulants approach zero and derive when full-drift inference collapses to the Gaussian polarity quotient.

literature_map.anchor_read: The Introduction and Conclusion of vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 motivate scale-invariant qualitative causal targets and explicitly name graph-level signs as future work. Theorem 4.2 turns individual-edge ambiguity into feasibility at a zero edge; Remark 5.1 describes a linear feasibility implementation. DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023 constructs the half-vectorized Lyapunov map, shows the two-cycle fiber is underdetermined, and proves global identifiability exactly for simple graphs when volatility is diagonal.
adjacent_threads: Hansen2025Trek gives power-series covariance expansions and acyclic variance inequalities, but cyclic formulas remain infinite and it does not analyze sign quotients of an inverse fiber.
AmendolaBoegeHolleringMisra2025 characterizes model equivalence for acyclic graphical continuous Lyapunov models, excluding the directed two-cycle used here.
ReckeHansen2026 obtains generic full drift identification from non-Gaussian higher cumulants; the present Gaussian experiment has covariance as its entire observable law.
DettlingDrtonKolar2024 studies Lyapunov-lasso support recovery, not exact compatibility of a known two-cycle's joint edge signs.
literature_map.occupation_check: No scanned paper states a necessary-and-sufficient product-sign certificate for unknown positive diagonal diffusion after fixing the common time-scale gauge, with post-gauge edge margins, a post-gauge norm cap, and strict-attainment branches.

literature_map.anchor_read: The two-cycle example of DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023 isolates a nontrivial linear fiber, while the model definition in vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 requires strictly positive diagonal diffusion. Neither proof distinguishes a closed quadratic-program minimizer from a legal interior-diffusion witness.
adjacent_threads: Hansen2025Trek supplies explicit covariance inequalities but does not classify strict inequalities along bounded cyclic fibers.
DettlingDrtonKolar2024 develops deterministic sample-covariance perturbation control around Lyapunov loss, without equality-active feasibility analysis.
BoegeBoegeHolleringMisra2025 studies conditional-independence structure of stationary diffusions, a different observable restriction from sector attainment.
literature_map.occupation_check: The exact destination pair, active-set completeness plus strict-diffusion topology for a bivariate Lyapunov sign sector, was not occupied in the bounded search.

literature_map.anchor_read: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 propagates sampling uncertainty through criterion inversion for identified sets. FangSantos2019 explains why ordinary bootstrap inference can fail for nondifferentiable maps and works through tangent-cone projections. Kaji2021 derives impossibility for weakly regular degree-zero parameters from regular local experiments.
adjacent_threads: vanSeeventerSalehkaleybar2026 defines only population signature sets and gives no sampling theorem.
FangSantos2019 supplies directional-differentiability machinery, but direct covariance-region inversion gives finite-sample coverage without differentiating the discontinuous polarity map.
Kaji2021 supplies the weak-identification interpretation but not the OU contact coordinate or Gaussian covariance metric.
ReckeHansen2026 derives asymptotic normality only after adding non-Gaussian higher-cumulant information.
literature_map.occupation_check: No closer result handles empty intersections caused by strict-diffusion nonclosure or proves both uniform singleton recovery and a matching local Gaussian obstruction for OU polarity sets.

novelty_justification: The closest published result is van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar's one-edge signature-set theory: its target is \(\operatorname{sign}(A_e)\), its decisive construction allows a single target edge to equal zero, and its graph-level extension is left open. Their work supplies the positive diagonal diffusion context, not the trace-one convention. The selected kernel first quotients the elementary common scaling \( (A,D)\mapsto(cA,cD)\) by choosing \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=1\); it then maps the observed covariance into \(\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21})\) under edge and drift-norm bounds \(\eta\) and \(M\) expressed in that normalized time unit. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen prove that a directed two-cycle destroys global drift injectivity when diagonal volatility is fixed, but they do not ask whether a nontrivial sign functional is constant on that fiber. The finite sector certificate, strict-attainment topology, equal-variance thresholds, and zero-diffusion contact are therefore new mathematical objects rather than a relabeling of either comparator. The inference layer is also absent from the OU sign literature: generic set inversion does not supply the measurable fallback or the contact-specific upper and lower recovery theory.
